questions.passage: Many schools are discovering that a small school garden can become an effective outdoor classroom. Students can observe how seeds germinate, measure the growth of plants and learn why soil, sunlight and water are important. A garden also gives them an opportunity to practise responsibility. Different groups may be asked to water plants, remove weeds, collect dry leaves for compost and record changes in a simple notebook. The activity connects textbook ideas with real experience. It can also improve the appearance of the school and provide a quiet place where students can observe birds and insects. The success of such a garden does not depend on expensive equipment. Careful planning, regular attention and cooperation are often more important. When students see the results of their own work, they understand that useful changes can begin with small and consistent efforts.
questions.question: Answer the following: (a) How can a school garden become an outdoor classroom? (b) Mention two responsibilities students may perform. (c) Why does the writer say that expensive equipment is not essential?
questions.model_answer: (a) A school garden becomes an outdoor classroom because students can observe germination, plant growth and the importance of soil, sunlight and water through direct experience. (b) They may water plants, remove weeds, collect leaves for compost and record changes. (c) The writer says expensive equipment is not essential because careful planning, regular attention and cooperation are more important for maintaining the garden.

questions.chapter: Unseen passage — main idea and details
questions.passage: Public libraries have changed considerably, but their purpose remains important. A modern library may provide printed books as well as newspapers, digital resources and quiet places for study. Some libraries organise reading programmes, storytelling sessions and workshops for children. Such activities can make reading a social experience and encourage young people to explore subjects beyond their school textbooks. Libraries are especially valuable to students who do not have a large collection of books at home. They provide access to information without requiring every family to purchase every resource. A library also teaches habits that are useful beyond examinations. Visitors learn to search for reliable information, compare ideas, take notes and respect shared spaces. In a time when information is available everywhere, the ability to select useful and trustworthy information is itself an important skill. For this reason, a library continues to be a place for learning, discovery and responsible use of knowledge.
questions.question: Answer the following: (a) Mention two resources or facilities a modern library may provide. (b) Why are libraries especially useful to some students? (c) What important skill does the passage say students need in the information age?
questions.model_answer: (a) A modern library may provide printed books, newspapers, digital resources and quiet study spaces. (b) Libraries are useful to students who do not have a large collection of books at home because they provide access to many resources. (c) Students need the ability to select useful and trustworthy information from the large amount of information available.

questions.passage: At first, the school bus stop was crowded and disorderly every morning. Students often stood too close to the road, and vehicles found it difficult to pass safely. A group of senior students discussed the problem with their teacher and suggested a simple plan. They marked a waiting area away from the road, placed a sign requesting students to stand in a line and took turns helping younger children. The change did not require much money or complicated equipment. What it required was cooperation and regular attention. Within a few weeks, the morning crowd became calmer. Younger students began following the example of the seniors, and drivers could move past the stop more safely. The experience taught the students that solving a community problem does not always begin with a large project. Sometimes a clear plan, responsible behaviour and willingness to cooperate are enough to create a useful improvement.
questions.question: Answer the following: (a) What problems existed at the bus stop? (b) What steps did the senior students take? (c) What lesson did the students learn from the experience?
questions.model_answer: (a) The bus stop was crowded and disorderly; students stood too close to the road and vehicles had difficulty passing safely. (b) The senior students marked a safe waiting area, put up a sign asking students to stand in line and helped younger children. (c) They learned that community problems can sometimes be solved through a clear plan, responsible behaviour and cooperation rather than an expensive project.

questions.passage: A habit of keeping a personal learning journal can help students become more aware of how they learn. The journal need not contain long entries. A student may record what was studied, which idea was difficult, what mistake was made and what should be revised later. After several weeks, these short notes can reveal patterns. A student may notice, for example, that vocabulary is forgotten when it is only read once, or that mathematics problems are easier after regular practice. This information can help the student change the method of study instead of simply spending more hours on the same method. The journal can also record small successes, such as completing a difficult chapter or improving a test score. Recognising progress can build confidence and encourage continued effort. In this way, a learning journal becomes more than a record of work; it becomes a tool for reflection, planning and improvement.
questions.question: Answer the following: (a) What four things may a student record in a learning journal? (b) How can the journal help a student change the method of study? (c) Why can recording small successes be useful?
questions.model_answer: (a) A student may record what was studied, difficult ideas, mistakes made and what needs revision. (b) The journal reveals patterns in learning, helping the student identify which methods work and change methods that are ineffective. (c) Recording small successes can build confidence and encourage the student to continue making an effort.

questions.passage: Clean surroundings are not created only by sweeping streets after waste has already accumulated. They depend greatly on what people do before waste becomes a problem. Households can separate recyclable material from other waste, carry reusable bags and avoid buying unnecessary packaged products. Schools can place clearly labelled bins and teach students why different kinds of waste need different treatment. Local communities can organise collection systems and keep public places free from litter. These measures work best when they become regular habits rather than occasional campaigns. Cleanliness also has a connection with health. Proper disposal reduces unpleasant smells, prevents some pests from multiplying and makes shared spaces safer and more pleasant. The responsibility therefore belongs to everyone who uses a street, classroom, market or public park. A clean environment is not simply the result of somebody else's work; it is the result of many people making careful choices every day.
questions.question: Answer the following: (a) Mention two ways households can reduce waste. (b) How can schools contribute to better waste management? (c) What is the central message of the passage?
questions.model_answer: (a) Households can separate recyclable waste, use reusable bags and avoid unnecessary packaged products. (b) Schools can provide labelled bins and teach students how different kinds of waste should be treated. (c) The central message is that cleanliness and responsible waste management depend on the regular choices and cooperation of everyone in a community.

questions.passage: A student preparing for a final examination decided to stop studying only the topics that felt easy. She made a list of all the chapters and marked each one as strong, developing or difficult. She then divided her available study time among the three groups. Strong topics received shorter revision sessions, while difficult topics received more frequent practice. After each week she tested herself without looking at the textbook and noted the areas in which she still made mistakes. Instead of becoming discouraged by the mistakes, she used them to decide what to revise next. As the examination approached, she had a clearer idea of her strengths and weaknesses. Her method did not make every topic equally easy, but it made her preparation more organised and purposeful. She also learned that honest self-assessment is more useful than repeatedly revising only the chapters she already knew well.
questions.question: Answer the following: (a) How did the student classify the chapters? (b) How did she use mistakes in her preparation? (c) What lesson did she learn about self-assessment?
questions.model_answer: (a) She classified the chapters as strong, developing or difficult. (b) She used mistakes to identify what she needed to revise and practise next. (c) She learned that honest self-assessment is more useful than repeatedly revising only the chapters she already knew well.

questions.question: Write an essay of about 18–20 sentences on 'The Role of Technology in Education'. Discuss advantages, responsible use and possible limitations.
questions.model_answer: Technology has become an important part of modern education. Digital resources can help students find information quickly and understand difficult ideas through videos, diagrams and interactive activities. Online dictionaries and educational platforms can also support independent learning. However, technology is useful only when it is used responsibly. Students should not allow games, social media or unnecessary browsing to distract them from their studies. They should also learn to check whether online information is reliable. Technology cannot completely replace teachers, books, discussion and real-life experience. A balanced approach is therefore necessary. When used with discipline and good guidance, technology can make learning more accessible, interesting and effective.

questions.question: Write an essay of about 18–20 sentences on 'Save Water, Save Life'. Include causes of wastage, practical measures and a conclusion.
questions.model_answer: Water is essential for every form of life, yet it is often wasted through careless habits. Leaking taps, unnecessary washing and excessive use in gardens can waste large quantities of water. People should repair leaks promptly and avoid leaving taps running. Rainwater harvesting can provide an additional source for suitable uses. Students can also spread awareness about saving water at home and at school. Communities should protect ponds, lakes and other local water sources from pollution. Saving water is not only a responsibility of governments; every individual has a role to play. Small daily changes become powerful when many people follow them. Therefore, we must use water carefully and protect it for future generations.

questions.question: Write an essay of about 18–20 sentences on 'Importance of Discipline in Student Life'.
questions.model_answer: Discipline helps students use their time and abilities effectively. It teaches them to follow a routine, complete work on time and respect rules. A disciplined student does not depend entirely on last-minute preparation. Regular study also reduces examination stress and improves confidence. Discipline does not mean giving up recreation or rest. It means balancing study, exercise, family time and leisure sensibly. Students who develop self-discipline can work towards long-term goals without constant reminders. The habit is useful not only in school but also in higher education and professional life. Therefore, discipline should be understood as a positive habit that helps students become responsible and independent.

questions.question: Write an essay of about 18–20 sentences on 'Trees: Our Natural Wealth'.
questions.model_answer: Trees are among the most valuable natural resources on earth. They provide shade, support wildlife, protect soil and contribute to cleaner air. They also make towns and villages cooler and more pleasant. Many people depend on trees for food, fuel, timber and other useful products. However, unnecessary cutting and loss of green spaces can damage the environment. Planting new trees is helpful, but protecting mature trees is equally important. Schools and communities can organise tree-care activities and protect local green spaces. Students can also avoid damaging young plants and encourage others to care for them. If people treat trees as a shared natural wealth rather than an unlimited resource, future generations will benefit. Protecting trees is therefore an investment in a healthier future.

questions.question: Write an essay of about 18–20 sentences on 'The Value of Sports and Games for Students'.
questions.model_answer: Sports and games are an important part of a balanced student life. Physical activity keeps the body active and can improve mood and concentration. Games also teach cooperation, patience and respect for rules. Team sports help students understand that success often depends on working with others. Individual activities can develop self-discipline and perseverance. Regular exercise can also reduce the unhealthy effects of sitting for long periods. Students should therefore make time for physical activity along with academic work. Schools can support this by providing opportunities for different sports and encouraging participation. Sports should not be seen only as competition; they are also a means of developing healthy habits and useful personal qualities.

questions.question: Write an essay of about 18–20 sentences on 'Road Safety: Everyone's Responsibility'.
questions.model_answer: Road safety is a shared responsibility. Pedestrians, cyclists, passengers and drivers must all follow safe practices. People should obey traffic signals, use safe crossing places and avoid using phones while crossing or driving. Wearing a helmet or seat belt can reduce the seriousness of injuries. Students should learn road-safety rules and encourage younger children to follow them. Drivers must respect speed limits and remain alert near schools and crowded areas. Authorities also have a role in maintaining signs, crossings and roads. Accidents can often be reduced when people combine awareness with responsible behaviour. Road safety is therefore not only a matter for traffic police; it is a daily responsibility for every member of the community.

questions.question: Write an essay of about 18–20 sentences on 'A Clean and Green School'.
questions.model_answer: A clean and green school creates a healthy and pleasant environment for learning. Clean classrooms help students concentrate and develop good habits. Trees, plants and small gardens can make the campus cooler and more attractive. Students can help by using bins correctly, avoiding litter and caring for plants. Schools can separate waste and encourage recycling where suitable. Water and electricity should also be used carefully. Cleanliness should not depend only on workers; students and teachers should cooperate. Regular awareness activities can turn these practices into habits. A clean and green school teaches an important lesson: caring for shared spaces is a form of responsibility. Such a campus benefits both present students and future generations.

questions.question: Write an essay of about 18–20 sentences on 'Reading as a Lifelong Habit'.
questions.model_answer: Reading can begin as a school activity and continue throughout life. It improves vocabulary, comprehension and the ability to understand different viewpoints. Reading stories can develop imagination, while biographies and informative books can increase knowledge. Newspapers and reliable articles can help readers understand the world around them. A regular reading habit also gives people a productive way to use free time. Students can begin with a few pages each day and gradually increase the amount they read. They can keep a list of interesting words and ideas. The purpose is not simply to finish many books but to develop curiosity and thoughtful understanding. A lifelong reading habit therefore supports learning long after formal education ends.

questions.question: Write an essay of about 18–20 sentences on 'The Importance of Time Management During Examinations'.
questions.model_answer: Time management is especially important during examinations. Students need to divide the available time among reading, answering and checking their work. Before writing, they should read the paper carefully and understand the marks allotted to each question. Easy questions may be answered first if that helps build confidence. Students should avoid spending too much time on one difficult question. Leaving a few minutes for revision can help them correct simple mistakes. Good time management begins before the examination through regular practice with timed papers. It reduces panic and helps students use their knowledge effectively. Therefore, managing time is an examination skill as important as knowing the subject matter.

questions.question: Write an essay of about 18–20 sentences on 'Responsible Use of Social Media by Students'.
questions.model_answer: Social media can help students communicate, share ideas and discover useful information, but it must be used responsibly. Students should protect personal information and avoid sharing material without checking its reliability. Excessive use can reduce study time and disturb sleep. Students should therefore set reasonable limits and avoid unnecessary scrolling while preparing for examinations. They should communicate respectfully and never use online platforms to insult or bully others. It is also important to remember that not everything posted online is true. A responsible user thinks before sharing, comments politely and protects privacy. When used with awareness and self-control, social media can be useful without becoming a distraction or a source of harm.

questions.question: Write a formal letter to the Editor of a newspaper about the need to control plastic waste in your locality.
questions.model_answer:
To
The Editor
[Newspaper Name]
[City]

Subject: Need to control plastic waste in our locality

Sir/Madam,

Through the columns of your newspaper, I wish to draw attention to the increasing use and careless disposal of plastic in our locality. Plastic waste is often found near roads, drains and public places. It blocks drainage and makes the surroundings unhealthy.

I request the concerned authorities to improve waste collection, encourage reusable alternatives and conduct awareness programmes. Residents should also be encouraged to avoid unnecessary single-use plastic.

I hope your newspaper will highlight this issue and encourage the public to act responsibly.

Yours faithfully,
[Name]

questions.question: Write a formal letter to the Municipal Commissioner requesting better street lighting in your locality.
questions.model_answer:
To
The Municipal Commissioner
[City/Municipality]

Subject: Request for better street lighting in our locality

Sir/Madam,

I am a resident of [locality] and wish to bring to your notice the inadequate street lighting in our area. Several lights are not functioning, making the roads difficult to use after sunset. This causes inconvenience to residents and creates safety concerns.

I request the municipality to inspect the street lights, repair the damaged fittings and install additional lights wherever necessary. Regular maintenance would also prevent the problem from recurring.

I hope prompt action will be taken in the interest of residents.

Yours faithfully,
[Name]

questions.question: Write a formal letter to the Headmaster/Headmistress requesting permission to organise a career-guidance programme for Class X students.
questions.model_answer:
To
The Headmaster/Headmistress
[School Name]

Subject: Request to organise a career-guidance programme

Sir/Madam,

We, the students of Class X, request permission to organise a career-guidance programme in our school. Many students are uncertain about the courses and career options available after Class X. A guidance session by a qualified counsellor or experienced professional would help us understand different opportunities.

We request permission to conduct the programme at a convenient time under the guidance of a teacher. We believe it will help students make informed decisions about their future.

Kindly grant us permission for the programme.

Yours obediently,
[Name]
Class X

questions.question: Write a formal letter to the Editor about the importance of maintaining public parks in towns and cities.
questions.model_answer:
To
The Editor
[Newspaper Name]
[City]

Subject: Need for proper maintenance of public parks

Sir/Madam,

I wish to draw attention to the poor maintenance of some public parks in our town. Broken benches, litter and damaged plants make these spaces less useful to residents. Parks provide places for exercise, relaxation and children's recreation, so they deserve regular care.

I request the municipal authorities to improve cleaning, maintain walking paths and protect trees and plants. Public awareness can also encourage residents to keep parks clean.

I hope your newspaper will highlight this matter and encourage timely action.

Yours faithfully,
[Name]

questions.question: Write a formal letter to the Headmaster/Headmistress requesting additional reference books for the school library.
questions.model_answer:
To
The Headmaster/Headmistress
[School Name]

Subject: Request for additional reference books

Sir/Madam,

I request the school to add more reference books to the library for Class X students. Students preparing for examinations would benefit from additional grammar books, dictionaries, question banks and subject-related reference material.

At present, the number of copies is limited, so several students cannot use the same resources at the same time. Adding suitable books would encourage independent study and regular reading.

Kindly consider our request and provide additional reference material if possible.

Yours obediently,
[Name]
Class X

questions.question: Write a formal letter to the concerned transport authority requesting a safe bus shelter near your school.
questions.model_answer:
To
The Concerned Transport Authority
[City]

Subject: Request for a safe bus shelter near our school

Sir/Madam,

I wish to request a bus shelter near our school because students and other passengers have to wait in the open. During rain and strong sunlight, the situation becomes uncomfortable. The absence of a designated waiting area can also create safety problems near the road.

I request the authority to inspect the location and provide a suitable shelter with adequate seating and safe access. A clear stopping point would also help buses and passengers.

I hope necessary action will be taken at the earliest.

Yours faithfully,
[Name]

questions.question: Write an informal letter to your friend describing how you are preparing for your final examination and asking about your friend's preparation.
questions.model_answer:
Dear Friend,

I hope you are well. I am writing to tell you about my preparation for the final examination. I have divided the syllabus into smaller portions and revise difficult topics more frequently. I also practise previous questions and take short tests to check my progress.

I am trying to manage my time carefully and keep the last few days for revision. How is your preparation going? Do write back and tell me about your study plan.

Yours lovingly,
[Name]

questions.question: Write an informal letter to your cousin inviting them to spend part of the vacation with your family.
questions.model_answer:
Dear Cousin,

I hope you are doing well. Our vacation is approaching, and I would be very happy if you could spend a few days with us. We are planning to visit some nearby places and spend time together at home.

It would be a wonderful opportunity for us to talk, play and enjoy the holidays together. Please discuss the plan with your parents and let me know when you can come.

Yours lovingly,
[Name]

questions.question: Write an informal letter to your friend telling them about a school activity that you enjoyed recently.
questions.model_answer:
Dear Friend,

I want to tell you about an interesting activity we had at school recently. Our class took part in a reading and presentation programme. We worked in small groups, selected topics and presented our ideas to the class.

I enjoyed the activity because everyone had a chance to speak and listen to others. It also helped me become more confident. I wish you had been there. I hope we can take part in a similar activity together sometime.

Yours lovingly,
[Name]

questions.question: Write an informal letter to your friend advising them to develop a regular reading habit.
questions.model_answer:
Dear Friend,

I am writing to suggest that you develop a regular reading habit. Reading even a few pages every day can improve vocabulary, comprehension and general knowledge. You could begin with stories or newspapers that interest you and gradually explore other books.

You can keep a small notebook for new words and interesting ideas. I am sure that regular reading will also help you in your school work. Try reading for twenty minutes each day and tell me how you feel after a few weeks.

Yours lovingly,
[Name]

questions.question: Write an informal letter to your friend describing a visit to a place of historical importance.
questions.model_answer:
Dear Friend,

Last week I visited a place of historical importance with my family. The visit was interesting because I saw old buildings and learned about the people and events connected with the place. A guide explained several important facts and showed us different parts of the site.

The visit helped me understand that history is more interesting when we see real places instead of only reading about them. I wish you had joined us. We should plan a visit together during the next vacation.

Yours lovingly,
[Name]

questions.question: Write an informal letter to your younger sibling encouraging them to balance study, exercise and recreation.
questions.model_answer:
Dear [Name],

I hope your studies are going well. I want to remind you that a healthy routine should include study, exercise and some recreation. Studying continuously without breaks can make you tired, while too much entertainment can affect your preparation.

Try making a simple daily timetable. Keep regular periods for study, take short breaks and spend some time playing or exercising. I am sure this balanced routine will help you feel healthier and study with greater concentration.

With love,
[Name]
